AbstractText.Label: CONTEXT
AbstractText.content: Hypercholesterolemia has significant cardiac consequences, since it is among the major risk factors of ischemic heart diseases.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: The aim was searching the cardioprotective effect of chemical constituents from the sea lettuce Ulva lactuca upon hypercholesterolemic regime in mice.

AbstractText.Label: MATERIAL AND METHODS
AbstractText.content: Mice were randomly divided into three groups: untreated group, hypercholesterolemic group, and mice receiving 1% cholesterol associated with U. lactuca ethanolic extract.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: In vitro study demonstrated that algal extract has antioxidant efficacy attributable to the presence of phenolic compounds. Additionally, the alga alleviated cardiotoxicity, as shown by the improvement of haematological parameters, white cell viability, heart oxidative stress, plasma biochemical parameters and index of atherogenesis. Gene expression of the proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α, IL-1β and IL-6 significantly decreased in the heart of U. lactuca supplemented hypercholesterolemic animals.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: It was established that the green alga, thanks to its bioactive compounds, effectively counteracts cardiotoxic effects of hypercholesterolemic regime.
